name: Royal National Lifeboat Institution (SoGive, 2020)
beneficiaries_note: The countries the model's summary names, sharing equally: United Kingdom, Ireland.
summary: Lifeboats, lifeguards and water-safety campaigns around the coasts of the UK and Ireland. SoGive's estimate of the RNLI's cost per life saved in 2019, from its annual report, rebuilt from SoGive's analysis.

source.title: The Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI): SoGive rating and analysis
source.license: No licence on the page. SoGive's data terms (sogive.org/doc/getourdata.html, archived September 2019): data for charity analysis is free with attribution to SoGive; use in apps needs a licence, free for low-intensity use, on condition that users are told the source of impact assessments with a link back to SoGive. This model cites SoGive and links its page.

resources.title: SoGive, RNLI analysis
resources.note: SoGive's charity page (its analysis text); SoGive publishes no spreadsheet for it, so the model is built from the figures stated in the text, each quoted on its row. Rated "Not Recommended (firm)"; the record was last modified on 15 October 2020.

resources.title: RNLI, Annual Report and Accounts 2019
resources.note: Costs from pp. 37 and 49, lives saved from pp. 5–10 (as cited by SoGive).

sections.title: Spending on rescue and safety work, 2019
From pounds per life to value per dollar
sections.explainer: charityevals' steps after SoGive's bottom line: SoGive's direct costs plus overheads (SoGive's own fuller figure), pounds to dollars, and each life saved valued like any other adult's death on the site (GiveWell's value, times the value-of-life slider).

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not the evaluator's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's pay below what they could earn elsewhere counts as an in-kind contribution and gets its share of the outcome. Off by default.

rows.label: Lives saved
rows.explainer: The RNLI's own count, taken at face value: a life counts as saved when the crew judge the person would have died without them. SoGive notes the lifeguards' preventive work may save more lives than are recorded, and that the 38,713 people aided (mostly not in danger of death) add a little; doubling the lives and counting the aid would still leave the RNLI far from its benchmark.

rows.label: Direct cost per life saved (£)
rows.explainer: SoGive: "Given the 385 lives saved, this gives a cost of over £420,000 per life saved in 2019 (and with overhead costs, this is closer to £500,000 per life saved)."

rows.label: Cost per life saved including overheads (£, SoGive)

source.title: SoGive, RNLI analysis and record
source.quote: and with overhead costs, this is closer to £500,000 per life saved
source.note: The exact figure, £497,662.34 per life saved, is the cost per life the SoGive app shows for the RNLI (record field costPerBeneficiary).

rows.explainer: SoGive's figure with overheads; a donation pays for fundraising and support costs too, so our view uses it. It implies £191.6m of spending in all (×385), which also covers the Bangladesh and flood rescue work left out of the lives count, so it slightly overstates the cost.

rows.label: Full cost relative to direct cost
US dollars per pound, 2019
rows.explainer: charityevals' step: SoGive's figure is in pounds; the site counts per dollar, so the pounds are converted at the year's average exchange rate (shared fact).

rows.label: Lives saved per dollar
Value of a life saved (units of value)
rows.explainer: GiveWell's value for averting the death of someone aged five or over, the site's default for an adult's death, times the value-of-life slider (Your values). SoGive counts lives, not years; those rescued are mostly adults.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for a UK charity that both delivers services and funds others: a little under half the cost is staff. Our judgment; we haven't seen this charity's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: UK charity staff earn somewhat less than in comparable private-sector jobs. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Volunteers' time, valued at wages, as a share of the cash cost
rows.explainer: Our judgment. Most lifeboat crew are unpaid volunteers on call; with credit by share of resources, their time is a contribution like staff's forgone pay and gets its share of the lives saved.

rows.label: Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay and volunteers' time count as part of the cost, and they get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: How much the next dollar does compared with the average dollar so far
rows.explainer: Your value, shared with every model built on an organisation's past average (Your values: "How much the next dollar does compared with the average dollar so far"): SoGive's figure is the RNLI's 2019 spending on lifeboats, lifeguards and safety campaigns over the lives it counts as saved that year, an average; the stations and campaigns already cover the UK and Irish coasts, so a further dollar saves fewer lives than the average dollar did. 50% by default (our judgment), from 18% to 100% (average = marginal). The evaluator view keeps 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar donated
rows.explainer: The figure per dollar above; with credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest). A marginal dollar is counted at the share of the past average you set (row above).
